name: X-linked Dyserythropoietic Anemia with Abnormal Platelets and Neutropenia
aliases: X-linked Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type with Thrombocytopenia and Neutropenia
X-linked Dyserythropoietic Anemia with Platelet and Neutrophil Abnormalities

criteria.description: Presence of marked dyserythropoiesis with multinuclear erythroblasts on bone marrow examination
Abnormal platelet morphology and thrombocytopenia detected on peripheral blood smear and platelet function tests
Chronic neutropenia confirmed by repeated complete blood counts
Identification of pathogenic variants in the implicated X-linked gene (e.g., GATA1 mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: dyserythropoiesis, abnormal platelets, and neutropenia
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and hematological features are definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic morphological abnormality diagnostic of dyserythropoiesis
searchTerms: red blood cells with multiple nuclei
immature red cells with several nuclei
bone marrow cells with many nuclei
low platelet count with abnormal platelets

common.symptomName: Mild to moderate anemia symptoms (e.g., pallor, exertional dyspnea)
Recurrent bacterial infections due to neutropenia
searchTerms: frequent bacterial infections due to low neutrophils
repeated infections from immune cell deficiency

common.symptomName: Easy bruising or petechiae due to thrombocytopenia
searchTerms: easy bruising and small skin bleeds

rare.symptomName: Bone pain due to marrow expansion

searchTerms: mild yellow skin from red blood cell breakdown
slight skin yellowing from blood cell destruction

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing thrombocytopenia and neutropenia
Bone marrow aspirate revealing multinuclear erythroblasts and dyserythropoiesis
Reduced neutrophil counts on repeated CBCs
Platelet function abnormalities on aggregation studies
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI may show mild splenomegaly or hepatomegaly
genetic: Pathogenic variants in X-linked genes such as GATA1 associated with dyserythropoiesis and platelet abnormalities
other: Normal or mildly elevated reticulocyte count
Absence of significant hemolysis markers in most cases

distinguishingFeatures: Distinct bone marrow morphology with internuclear chromatin bridges
Absence of neutropenia and platelet abnormalities
Microthrombocytopenia rather than abnormal platelet morphology

redFlags: Severe neutropenia with recurrent life-threatening infections
